newsitem.title: USA: ALPINE SKIING-STROBL LEADS WORLD CUP GIANT SLALOM FIRST RUN.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-STROBL LEADS WORLD CUP GIANT SLALOM FIRST RUN.

text.p: Austrian Josef Strobl, taking advantage of a break in light snow and fog Monday, was fastest in the first run of a men's World Cup giant slalom.

Strobl, skiing 20th, covered the 50-gate run in one minute, 15.25 seconds to take a half-second lead over Michael Von Gruenigen of Switzerland (1:15.77). Rising Italian star Matteo Nana was third in 1:15.96.

The second giant slalom of the season, postponed from last Friday due to rain, began in light snow and changing weather conditions. Early skiers raced at the top of the course through fog, which rolled in and out during the remainder of the run at Park City Ski Area.
